en: Section B interview.
zh: B节：访谈。

en: In this section, you will hear one interview.
zh: 在这一节中，你将听到一段访谈。

en: The interview will be divided into two parts.
zh: 这段访谈分为两部分。

en: At the end of each part, five questions will be asked about what was said.
zh: 每部分结束后，将就刚才所说的内容提出五个问题。

en: Both the interview and the questions will be spoken once only.
zh: 访谈和问题都只读一遍。

en: After each question, there will be a ten-second pause.
zh: 每个问题之后会有十秒钟的停顿。

en: During the pause, you should read the four choices of A, B, C, and D and mark the best answer to each question on answer sheet 2.
zh: 请利用停顿时间阅读A、B、C、D四个选项，并在答题卡二上标出每题的最佳答案。

en: You have 30 seconds to preview the choices.
zh: 你有三十秒钟预览选项。

en: Now listen to part one of the interview.
zh: 现在请听访谈的第一部分。

en: Questions one to five are based on part one of the interview.
zh: 第1至5题根据访谈的第一部分提问。

en: Maureen McLane is a poet and critic.
zh: 莫琳·麦克莱恩是一位诗人和评论家。

en: After her undergraduate studies in American history and literature, she studied English literature on a scholarship before earning her Ph.D. at the University of Chicago.
zh: 她本科时学习美国历史和文学，随后获得奖学金学习英国文学，之后在芝加哥大学取得博士学位。

en: In addition to academic publications on British romanticism, Maureen McLane has written a number of memoirs and criticism.
zh: 除了有关英国浪漫主义的学术著作，莫琳·麦克莱恩还写过一些回忆录和评论作品。

en: One of them, My Poets, became a finalist for the 2012 National Book Critics Circle Award in autobiography.
zh: 其中一本《我的诗人》，入围了二〇一二年美国国家书评人协会奖的自传类奖项。

en: And her most recent collection of poetry, This Blue, was a finalist for the 2014 National Book Award.
zh: 她最近出版的诗集《这片蓝》，也入围了二〇一四年美国国家图书奖。

en: Today, we have Maureen McLane, now professor of English at New York University, with us on the radio show.
zh: 今天，我们请到了现任纽约大学英语教授莫琳·麦克莱恩，做客本台广播节目。

en: Good evening, Maureen.
zh: 晚上好，莫琳。

en: Good evening!
zh: 晚上好！

en: Now, can you tell us when you first began to read poetry?
zh: 您能告诉我们，您最早是什么时候开始读诗的吗？

en: I would probably say, in my high school days.
zh: 我想应该是在高中时期。

en: Of course, there had been some other things in the environment in my childhood before high school,
zh: 当然，在高中之前，我童年时的生活环境中也有其他相关事物，

en: like nursery rhymes, hymns, my mother’s playing piano and guitar, poems my father might come out with.
zh: 比如童谣、赞美诗、母亲弹奏钢琴和吉他，以及父亲随口念出的诗句。

en: But in terms of reading poetry, it really came about through high school.
zh: 但是，真正开始阅读诗歌，还是在高中阶段。

en: Literature classes in general were very stimulating to me.
zh: 总的来说，文学课对我很有启发。

en: You begin one section of My Poets by talking about the lecture course you took in your freshman year with Helen Vendler,
zh: 在《我的诗人》的一个章节开头，您谈到了大一时上的海伦·文德勒的讲座课，

en: and the poetry section you had with William Corbett.
zh: 以及威廉·科贝特教授的诗歌课。

en: Were there other teachers who were important to you?
zh: 还有其他对您很重要的老师吗？

en: Well, there were several people important to me who weren't poetry people at all — they were historians or professors of music.
zh: 对我很重要的几个人，完全不是诗歌界人士，而是历史学家或音乐教授。

en: Oh, that’s interesting.
zh: 哦，这很有意思。

en: I had a wonderful tutor, now a professor of English at the University of Chicago, Janice Knight.
zh: 我有过一位很出色的导师，贾妮丝·奈特，她现在是芝加哥大学的英语教授。

en: Janice was and is a scholar of colonial America, but she also knew a lot about a certain line in American poetry.
zh: 贾妮丝过去和现在一直是一位研究殖民地时期美国的学者，但她也很熟悉美国诗歌的某一流派。

en: She introduced me to Susan Howe’s work.
zh: 她让我接触到了苏珊·豪的作品。

en: I mean, those people became important to me in various ways.
zh: 我的意思是，这些人以不同的方式对我产生了重要影响。

en: I almost feel as if in the end the poets themselves are the most important teachers.
zh: 我几乎觉得，到头来，诗人本人就是最重要的老师。

en: I do think that if you bend towards becoming a writer, at the end of the day, it’s writing that teaches you, I mean, other writers’ works.
zh: 我确实认为，如果你倾向于成为一名作家，归根结底，教会你写作的是写作本身；我是指其他作家的作品。
vocabulary: at the end of the day

en: You were an undergraduate at Harvard, and then you returned to teach there.
zh: 您在哈佛读过本科，后来又回到那里任教。

en: What was that like?
zh: 那是一种怎样的体验？

en: When I returned, I was at a very different phase of life.
zh: 回去的时候，我已处于人生中一个很不一样的阶段。

en: Being back as a professor, Cambridge, where Harvard University is, was very different —
zh: 以教授的身份重返校园时，哈佛大学所在的剑桥市已经很不一样了：

en: it was much more commercialized and cleaned-up than when I was an undergrad.
zh: 与我读本科时相比，那里商业化程度更高，环境也更整洁。

en: I liked being near Fresh Pond, and going to Walden.
zh: 我喜欢住在弗雷什池附近，也喜欢去瓦尔登。

en: I felt like I was getting to know New England a little bit better, in a way that was very different from when I was 18.
zh: 我觉得自己更加了解新英格兰了，而这种了解方式与我十八岁时很不一样。

en: I liked that, and I was more aware of the environment,
zh: 我很喜欢这种体验，也更加留意周围的环境。

en: You write in My Poets about the power of listening to “poetry fans read those poems or works they are committed to.”
zh: 您在《我的诗人》中谈到了聆听诗歌爱好者朗读他们倾心的诗歌或作品所具有的力量。

en: Is this an important teaching tool for you? .
zh: 这对您来说是一种重要的教学工具吗？

en: I definitely bring recordings to class.
zh: 我一定会把录音带到课堂上。

en: Recordings offer a great way to refocus one’s attention on the poem.
zh: 录音是让人重新把注意力集中到诗歌上的一种很好的方式。

en: I feel like it’s definitely a zone for encounter, a zone that’s really powerful.
zh: 我觉得，这无疑是一个让人相遇、与诗歌接触的空间，是一个非常有力量的空间。

en: I also think there is an inner ear, which is much more relevant to my sense of poetry than actual vocalization.
zh: 我还认为存在一种“内在的听觉”，与实际发声相比，它和我对诗歌的感知更为相关。

en: Some people are very attuned to this ear.
zh: 有些人对这种内在听觉非常敏感。

en: For example, they compose in their minds, maybe reciting aloud, and only at the end do they write things down.
zh: 例如，他们会先在脑中创作，也许会大声念出来，直到最后才把内容写下来。

en: So, I do think there’s an inner ear that is activated when one writes.
zh: 所以，我确实认为，人在写作时，会激活一种内在听觉。

en: Or at least for me.
zh: 至少对我来说是这样。

en: And that is as loud, as audible, as our conversation right now.
zh: 而且，它就像我们现在的交谈一样响亮、一样清晰可闻。

en: This is the end of part one of the interview.
zh: 访谈的第一部分到此结束。
